problem: DAS is presented next to the 8085 rotate and CMA instructions, so a student concludes the 8085 has DAS. The 8085 has only DAA; DAS is an 8086 instruction. Trap 3 ('DAA ... and DAS only after BCD subtraction ... On the 8051, DA A is used only after addition') repeats the implication that DAS belongs to this 8085 family.
fix: Say plainly: 'The 8085 has DAA only; it has no decimal-adjust instruction for subtraction. DAS is an 8086 instruction.' In trap 3 write: 'On the 8085 only DAA exists. On the 8086, DAA follows BCD addition and DAS follows BCD subtraction. The 8051 has DA A and uses it only after addition.'

problem: 'The 8086 has bit test and modify forms' is wrong. BT, BTS, BTR and BTC arrived with the 80386 and later. The 8086 has only TEST (an AND that sets flags and discards the result).
fix: Write: 'the 8086 has TEST, which ANDs two operands only to set flags; bit test and modify instructions (BT, BTS, BTR, BTC) come with the 386 and later.'

problem: 'Each instruction takes operands, computes a result, writes it back, and updates flags' overgeneralises. CMP and CPI compute but do not write back. INR and DCR never touch C, INX and DCX touch no flags. A student may expect every instruction to behave like ADD.
fix: Add one clause: 'Most write a result back and update flags; compare instructions only set flags, and INR/DCR and INX/DCX leave carry (or all flags) untouched.'

problem: AC is defined only as 'carry from bit 3 to bit 4'. In subtraction AC means a borrow from bit 4, which the chapter never says, though it uses SUB in quiz Q7.
fix: Add: 'in subtraction AC = 1 means a borrow from bit 4, just as C = 1 means a borrow from bit 8.'

where: Section 2, first line of the rotate group
problem: 'Rotates move bits through carry' is true for RAL and RAR only. RLC and RRC rotate the accumulator circularly and merely copy the shifted-out bit into C; the old C does not enter.
fix: Write: 'RAL and RAR move bits through carry; RLC and RRC rotate A circularly and also copy the bit that falls off into C.'

problem: The correction condition is misstated. DAA adds 60H when the high nibble is greater than 9 or CY was set, not when AC was set. As written, '06H or 60H when a nibble exceeded 9 or AC was set' wrongly ties 60H to AC.
fix: Reword: 'DAA adds 06H if the low nibble is greater than 9 or AC = 1, and adds 60H if the high nibble is greater than 9 or CY = 1 (both can apply, giving 66H). Binary addition has no BCD nibble rule, so DAA would corrupt it.'

problem: 'DIV and IDIV ... do not set flags like ADD' can be read as 'flags are left unchanged'. On the 8086 the flags after DIV/IDIV are undefined, not preserved.
fix: Write: 'DIV and IDIV leave all flags undefined; do not test a flag after them. MUL and IMUL set only CF and OF (with SF, ZF, AF, PF undefined).'.
